summary: Is the JSON literal null meant to be refused too? No test covers it, and DecodeRendered returns no error for it.
evidence: The function's comment states that a document which is not an object of strings is refused rather than read as empty. The one test of the refusal, internal/draft/rendered_test.go:57, passes {"f1": 7}, whose value is of the wrong type. summary: No fixture puts an added line before the first removed line of the chosen hunk, so the rule that added lines consume no pre-image line is never exercised and a derivation that counted them would name the wrong head line.
evidence: Target walks the chosen hunk's body and advances `line` only on a context marker (target.go:109-110), leaving added lines to consume nothing; the derived `path:line` is what §5.5 stores as a mutation probe's target and what §6.2.2 has a `probed` record's evidence point at. Every case in TestTheMutationTargetIsDerivedFromThePatchAlone (internal/probe/target_test.go:23) that reaches the `-` return places its added lines after the removal: "a replaced line gives its pre-image number" is ` `, ` `, `-`, `+`; "a -U0 hunk names the line it removes" is `-`, `+`; "a removed line deeper in a hunk counts the context above it" holds no `+` at all. The one fixture with a `+` ahead of other body lines, "an add-only hunk with context names its first pre-image line", holds no `-`, so it returns chosen.BaseStart and never reads `line`. A hunk shaped ` a`, `+inserted`, ` b`, `-c` — one insertion and one removal in the same hunk, which git writes routinely — reaches no test in this file, so if `case ' '` were widened to `case ' ', '+'` the target would move one line past the code the patch removes and no assertion in internal/probe would change. I could not run the suite here, so this is a suspicion from reading; x36701 applies exactly that mutation and settles it.

summary: Two hunks sharing a pre-image start are ordered by the patch's own layout, which the tie-break's strict `<` never overrides, and only one of the two spellings is tested.
evidence: Target's doc says the order is fixed "so every spelling of the same change derives the same target, and rewriting the patch's layout buys nothing" (target.go:48-51). The tie-break at target.go:92-93 keeps the incumbent when two hunks of one file share BaseStart, so at a tie the winner is whichever the patch wrote first. TestTheMutationTargetIsDerivedFromThePatchAlone's "an insertion sharing a removal's start does not take the target from it" (internal/probe/target_test.go:74) exercises one spelling — `@@ -41 +41 @@` then `@@ -41,0 +43,1 @@` — and expects "app.go:41". Reading the other spelling through the same code: the zero-pre-image-line hunk is chosen first, the second hunk's 41 < 41 is false so it is not displaced, the body holds only `+added`, and BaseLines == 0 sends the call to the refusal at target.go:113. The same change spelled the other way therefore yields a TargetError rather than app.go:41, and the patch here is the agent's own (§5.3.1), which is the reordering this function was written to make worthless. Every other ordering dimension in that test is asserted from both sides — the hunks that descend and ascend, the files that descend and ascend — and the tie is the one that is not. I could not run the suite here; x36702 adds the missing case.
